title: Vectors in images

draft.title: Vectors in images
card: A vector is a line in an image that leads the viewer's eye in a direction. The line can be real or imagined.
Vectors can be a pointing arm, a road, a fence, a river or the direction a person is looking. A gaze is an imagined line from the eyes to what they see.
Image creators use vectors to lead the eye to what they want noticed. The viewer often follows the line without thinking about it.
To find a vector, ask where the lines in the image point. The place they lead to is often the most important part of the image.
draft.remember: Vectors are lines that steer the eye to what the creator wants seen.

a.q: A poster shows a girl on a hill, looking at a small kite in the sky. What is the vector that leads the viewer to the kite?
opts: The line of the girl's gaze
The words printed below the poster
a.why: A gaze is an imagined line from the eyes to what a person is looking at, so it leads the viewer to the kite. The hill is a shape in the image, but it is not a line that points to the kite.
a.clue: Think of an imagined line from the girl to the kite.

b.q: An ad for a beach resort shows a long jetty running from the front of the image to a small hut at the far end. What does the jetty do?
opts: It leads the viewer's eye to the hut
It makes the hut seem close to the viewer
It shows the viewer how deep the water is
It tells the viewer the hut is not important
b.why: The jetty is a line that runs towards the hut, so it acts as a vector and draws the eye there. It does not make the hut seem close, because the hut is at the far end of the line.
b.clue: Follow the line of the jetty with your eye.

a.best: The line of the girl's gaze

b.best: It leads the viewer's eye to the hut
